answer: A random audit lottery with doubling fines costs 100 clones $8,100 while one honest agent risks $50. Each epoch a seeded lottery triggers a gale sweeping 5% of agents holding $50 deposits. Each swept agent faces raven auditors checking it against the glacier of past attestations, flagging any mismatch. Fines double per sibling caught in the same sweep, so five linked clones pay $100, $200, $400, $800 and $1,600. The farm locks $5,000 and bleeds $3,100 per sweep while the honest agent gets its $50 back. Like a market check where each stall caught selling fakes pays double the last fine.
